Gene Description

SKP1 (S-phase kinase-associated protein 1, p19skp1) is the small, highly conserved adaptor subunit of SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein) cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligases, the largest family of E3s in human cells. It is a 163-residue protein with an N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region that binds the first cullin repeat at the N-terminus of CUL1, and a helical, conformationally adaptable C-terminal region - with two mobile loops and a partly formed final helix - that clamps the ~40-residue F-box motif. Through that pair of contacts SKP1 tethers any one of the roughly 69 human F-box substrate receptors (SKP2, BTRC/FBXW11 beta-TrCP, FBXW7, cyclin F/CCNF, FBXL3, FBXL5, FBXO7, FBXO9, FBXO31 and others) to the CUL1-RBX1 catalytic core, where RBX1 recruits a ubiquitin-charged E2 (CDC34/UBE2R, UBE2D). SKP1 has no catalytic activity and forms no ubiquitin thioester: it contributes the geometry that brings a receptor-bound substrate within reach of the E2, and substrate choice rests entirely with the F-box protein. The assembled ligases build mainly K48-linked chains that commit substrates to the 26S proteasome - Thr187-phosphorylated p27/CDKN1B via SCF(SKP2) at the G1/S transition, IkappaB-alpha, beta-catenin, EMI1, CDC25A and NFE2L2 via SCF(beta-TrCP), cyclin E, MYC, NOTCH and WDR5 via SCF(FBXW7), CP110 and E2F1 via SCF(cyclin F), the cryptochromes via SCF(FBXL3)/SCF(FBXL21), and IRP2 via SCF(FBXL5). The same adaptor serves ligases built on other scaffolds and, in some cases, without a cullin at all: it is a core subunit of the CRL7(FBXW8) assembly and of the mitochondrial CUL1-RING(FBXL4) ligase, and in the CUL1-independent MYCBP2/PAM-FBXO45-SKP1 ligase it goes beyond scaffolding to strengthen the receptor's grip on its substrate NMNAT2. Independently of ubiquitination, SKP1 binding masks nuclear export signals that lie within the F-box of FBXO7 and a sixth of other F-box proteins, retaining them in the nucleus. SKP1 acts in the nucleus and nucleoplasm, in the cytosol, on chromatin as part of the KDM2B-SKP1 module of PRC1.1 variant Polycomb complexes, and at centrosomes, where it is present on nearly all purified centriole doublets. Because an adequate pool of SKP1 is needed to assemble the whole SCF repertoire, its depletion stabilises cyclin E1 and produces replication stress, micronuclei and chromosome instability.

PMID:11961546
Structure of the Cul1-Rbx1-Skp1-F boxSkp2 SCF ubiquitin liga... 		ACCEPT
Summary: SCF(SKP2), assembled on SKP1, ubiquitinates Thr187-phosphorylated p27/CDKN1B, releasing cyclin E/A-CDK2 activity and committing the cell to S phase; the SCF(SKP2) structure defines how SKP1 carries SKP2.
Reason: Core process: the p27 switch at the G1/S transition is the canonical output of an SCF ligase, SKP1 performs the adaptor work in that ligase, and this matches the annotations kept on CUL1, RBX1 and SKP2. Human SKP1 depletion stabilises cyclin E1 and causes replication stress, consistent with a requirement at this transition.

Summary: SCF ligases containing SKP1 build polyubiquitin chains on receptor-bound substrates; the beta-TrCP1-SKP1-beta-catenin structure led to the model in which SCF raises the effective concentration of the substrate lysine at the E2 active site.

GO_REF:0000107 		KEEP AS NON CORE
Summary: Ortholog transfer from mouse Skp1 (UniProtKB:Q9WTX5), which carries an IDA annotation to the centromeric chromosome region from a meiotic study; no human-cell evidence supports this location directly.
Reason: The source is a mouse experimental annotation, transferred by Ensembl Compara, and the orthologs are essentially identical, so the transfer is sound and should not be overruled. But a meiotic centromeric pool is a stage-restricted context rather than part of the core adaptor function, so it is kept as non-core.

ATF4 degradation relies on a phosphorylation-dependent inter... 		MODIFY
Summary: SKP1 binds FBXW2, the WD40 receptor for GCM1 and SKP2 (FBXW2) through the ~40-residue F-box motif, forming the SKP1-FBXW2 substrate-receptor module; evidence from SCF(beta-TrCP)-dependent ATF4 degradation, with FBXW2 assayed alongside beta-TrCP.
Reason: The informative molecular function behind this interaction is F-box domain binding (GO:1990444): the C-terminal helices of SKP1 dock the F-box motif of the receptor, which is how SKP1 tethers FBXW2 to CUL1-RBX1 (ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity, GO:0160072). Bare protein binding does not capture this.
Proposed replacements: F-box domain binding ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity

Summary: SKP1 binds FBXW7, the WD40 receptor for cyclin E, MYC, NOTCH and WDR5 (FBXW7) through the ~40-residue F-box motif, forming the SKP1-FBXW7 substrate-receptor module; evidence from the STYX study, in which STYX competes with SKP1 for the F-box of FBXW7.
Reason: The informative molecular function behind this interaction is F-box domain binding (GO:1990444): the C-terminal helices of SKP1 dock the F-box motif of the receptor, which is how SKP1 tethers FBXW7 to CUL1-RBX1 (ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity, GO:0160072). Bare protein binding does not capture this.
Proposed replacements: F-box domain binding ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity

Dimerization quality control ensures neuronal development an... 		MODIFY
Summary: SKP1 binds FBXL17, the dimerisation-quality-control receptor for BTB proteins (FBXL17) through the ~40-residue F-box motif, forming the SKP1-FBXL17 substrate-receptor module; evidence from the FBXL17 dimerisation-quality-control study.
Reason: The informative molecular function behind this interaction is F-box domain binding (GO:1990444): the C-terminal helices of SKP1 dock the F-box motif of the receptor, which is how SKP1 tethers FBXL17 to CUL1-RBX1 (ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity, GO:0160072). Bare protein binding does not capture this.
Proposed replacements: F-box domain binding ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:30190310
Underscoring the physiological importance of DQC, SCFFBXL17 is required for the differentiation, function, and survival of neural crest and neuronal cells.

KDM2B Overexpression Facilitates Lytic De Novo KSHV Infectio... 		MODIFY
Summary: SKP1 binds KDM2B/FBXL10, an F-box histone demethylase and PRC1.1 subunit (KDM2B) through the ~40-residue F-box motif, forming the SKP1-KDM2B substrate-receptor module; evidence from the KDM2B/KSHV study showing KDM2B binds the SCF complex via its F-box.
Reason: The informative molecular function behind this interaction is F-box domain binding (GO:1990444): the C-terminal helices of SKP1 dock the F-box motif of the receptor, which is how SKP1 tethers KDM2B to CUL1-RBX1 (ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity, GO:0160072). Bare protein binding does not capture this.
Proposed replacements: F-box domain binding ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:33692209
This effect is dependent upon the binding of KDM2B to the SKP1-CUL1-F-box (SCF) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex via its F-box domain.
file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt
In the SCF complex, serves as an adapter that links the F-box protein to CUL1.
file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
Human SKP1 contains an N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region participating in CUL1 association and a helical, conformationally adaptable C-terminal region that binds F-box domains.

Summary: Nuclear pool of SKP1, where SCF ligases act on nuclear substrates (p27/CDKN1B, cyclin E, MYC, NICD, CRY, RPA194, WDR5) and where SKP1 retains F-box proteins such as FBXO7. Inferred at the SKP1-family ancestral node from the experimental annotations of its descendants, including human P63208 itself.
Reason: Core location. The PAINT curator placed this assertion at the ancestral node PANTHER:PTN000126179 after reading the experimental annotations of the extant SKP1 family, and human P63208 appears among the descendant evidences precisely because it carries direct experimental support - that is expected, not circular. Nuclear SCF activity is independently supported by immunofluorescence and by the nuclear substrate set.

We propose that this competitive binding allowed Fbxo7 to accumulate within the nucleus starting at the G1/S transition

Summary: SKP1 is required for, and forms part of, the SCF ligases that ubiquitinate receptor-selected substrates for proteasomal degradation. Inferred at the SKP1-family ancestral node PANTHER:PTN000126179 from experimentally annotated descendants in fly, mouse, fission yeast, budding yeast and human.
Reason: Core process: every SCF ligase that SKP1 serves ends in proteasomal destruction of a receptor-selected substrate, and SKP1 performs part of the work of that process - it holds the receptor, and therefore the substrate, in register with the RBX1-bound E2. The claim is about the shared core subunit rather than any one receptor, which is exactly the level at which this term sits. The PAINT curator placed this assertion at the ancestral node PANTHER:PTN000126179 after reading the experimental annotations of the extant SKP1 family, and human P63208 appears among the descendant evidences precisely because it carries direct experimental support - that is expected, not circular.

These are functions of particular SCF assemblies; SKP1 enables them but is not the substrate-recognition determinant.

Core Functions

Adaptor of SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box-RBX1) cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases: the N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region binds the CUL1 N-terminal cullin repeat while the adaptable C-terminal helices clamp the F-box motif of one of ~69 interchangeable substrate receptors, holding the receptor-bound substrate in register with the ubiquitin-charged E2 delivered by RBX1. SKP1 performs no chemistry itself; it supplies the connection and the geometry through which mainly K48-linked chains are built on receptor-selected substrates, such as Thr187-phosphorylated p27/CDKN1B via SCF(SKP2) at the G1/S transition.

Nuclear retention of F-box proteins through the same F-box contact: because the leucine-rich nuclear export signal of FBXO7 and of more than ten other F-box proteins is embedded in the F-box domain, SKP1 binding physically occludes it and prevents exportin 1/CRM1 engagement, so the receptor accumulates in the nucleus from the G1/S transition onwards. SKP1 occupancy therefore sets where a subset of SCF ligases can assemble and act.

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: Should the ~265 GO:0005515 rows recording SKP1 with individual F-box proteins be re-curated as F-box domain binding (GO:1990444) plus SCF complex membership, or captured in GO-CAM as the receptor arm of each ligase activity, rather than as bare protein binding on the invariant adaptor?

Q: Where should the boundary lie between GO:0160072 (scaffold activity, what SKP1 does) and GO:1990756 (ligase-substrate adaptor activity, what the F-box protein does)? Both are currently annotated to SKP1 by IDA from the same beta-TrCP1-SKP1-beta-catenin structure, which shows the substrate bound by the receptor.

Q: Which receptor-specific outputs (circadian period, iron sensing, TORC1 signalling, xenophagy, mitophagy, ciliogenesis, neuromuscular synapse assembly) should be annotated to SKP1 at all, given that a single adaptor serves ~69 receptors and supports opposite-sign outputs through different ones?

Q: Is the substrate-binding enhancement seen for SKP1 in the PAM/FBXO45 ligase a general property of SKP1-receptor pairs - so that GO:0140677 would apply across SCF - or specific to the CUL1-independent complex in which it was demonstrated?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Measure substrate affinity and ubiquitination kinetics for purified receptor-substrate pairs from each F-box subfamily (SKP2-p27 with CKS1, BTRC-IkappaB-alpha phosphopeptide, FBXW7-cyclin E degron, FBXL3-CRY2) with and without SKP1, by surface plasmon resonance or ITC alongside single-turnover ubiquitin transfer, using an SCF core lacking SKP1 as the comparator.

Hypothesis: SKP1 contributes more than passive tethering across the SCF family, measurably increasing the affinity of F-box receptors for their substrates as it does for FBXO45-NMNAT2.

Type: quantitative binding and single-turnover kinetics with reconstituted ligases

Experiment: Introduce loop-2 and H7 substitutions and disulfide staples into SKP1, rescue SKP1-depleted cells with each allele, and compare the bound F-box proteome by quantitative interaction proteomics and the stability of a substrate panel (p27, cyclin E, IkappaB-alpha, CRY2, IRP2, CP110) by pulse-chase.

Hypothesis: The mobile C-terminal loops and partly formed H7 helix of SKP1 are what allow one adaptor to accept structurally diverse F-box domains, so rigidifying them should restrict the receptor repertoire rather than abolish ligase activity.

Type: structure-guided mutational rescue with interaction and degradation proteomics

Experiment: Compare SKP1 alleles that bind F-box domains but cannot bind CUL1 with wild-type SKP1 in SKP1-degron cells, scoring nuclear/cytoplasmic partitioning of FBXO7 and other NES-in-F-box receptors by imaging and fractionation, and separating that readout from substrate turnover measured in parallel.

Hypothesis: Nuclear retention of F-box proteins by SKP1 occupancy, not ubiquitination, accounts for part of the SKP1 loss-of-function phenotype.

Type: separation-of-function rescue with compartment-resolved imaging

Experiment: Quantify SKP1 at centrosomes by expansion microscopy and purified-centrosome proteomics in cells depleted of cyclin F, FBXW5 or FBXL13 individually and in combination, testing whether the pool collapses receptor by receptor or persists independently.

Hypothesis: The centrosomal pool of SKP1 is recruited by specific receptors rather than by an intrinsic centrosomal determinant in SKP1.

Type: quantitative imaging and organelle proteomics with receptor depletion

Human SKP1 (UniProt P63208): Functional-Annotation Research Report

Executive summary

Human SKP1 is a small, conserved intracellular adaptor protein whose best-established function is to connect the CUL1 scaffold of SCF Cullin–RING E3 ubiquitin ligases to interchangeable F-box substrate receptors. SKP1 is not an enzyme, does not itself select degradation substrates, and should not be confused with SKP2, which is one particular F-box substrate receptor. Through this architectural role, SKP1 enables ubiquitination of proteins governing the cell cycle, DNA replication and repair, centrosome duplication, mitosis, apoptosis, and signal transduction. Its experimentally supported locations include cytoplasm, nucleus, and centrosomes. The strongest recent development is a 2024 chemical-biology study showing that SKP1 can itself be recruited by heterobifunctional degraders to eliminate neo-substrates such as BRD4 and androgen receptor; this remains preclinical.

1. Mandatory identity verification

The requested target is correctly identified as human S-phase kinase-associated protein 1, gene SKP1, UniProt P63208. The literature describes a prototypic 163-amino-acid protein and historical names including p19, OCP2, and TCEB1L, consistent with the supplied UniProt record; the human gene is located at 5q31.1. A shorter 160-aa transcript product has also been described, although the 163-aa form is the principal experimentally characterized species. (hussain2022asmallmoleculeskp1 pages 1-2, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 1-2, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 2-4)

The supplied InterPro assignments—SKP1, SKP1-like, SKP1 dimerization-like, and SKP1/BTB/POZ superfamily—are concordant with structural literature. Human SKP1 contains an N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region participating in CUL1 association and a helical, conformationally adaptable C-terminal region that binds F-box domains. (bhattacharya2022disorderinthe pages 20-23, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 2-4)

Ambiguity control: SKP1 is not SKP2. SKP2 is an F-box substrate receptor that binds SKP1 in the SCF^SKP2 complex; papers about SKP2 inhibition or SKP2-regulated substrates do not by themselves establish a direct function of SKP1. Likewise, glycosylation and oxygen-sensing mechanisms reported for Dictyostelium, plant, fungal, or protist Skp1 proteins cannot automatically be assigned to human P63208. Only explicitly relevant comparative findings are used here. (thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 4-5, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 2-4, bhattacharya2022disorderinthe pages 35-38)

2. Primary molecular function

2.1 Non-catalytic adaptor in SCF ubiquitin ligases

The canonical SCF complex comprises SKP1–CUL1–F-box protein–RBX1. CUL1 is the elongated scaffold; RBX1 recruits the ubiquitin-charged E2 machinery; SKP1 bridges CUL1 to an interchangeable F-box receptor; and the F-box receptor binds the substrate. Consequently, SKP1 provides structural connectivity rather than catalytic chemistry. It has no established intrinsic enzymatic reaction, catalytic substrate, or transporter function. (thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 1-2, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 4-5, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 2-4)

Substrate specificity resides primarily in the variable F-box protein. Mammals encode approximately 69 F-box proteins, grouped broadly into FBXW, FBXL, and FBXO families. The receptor’s substrate-binding domain recognizes a target—frequently through a regulated degron—while its F-box domain docks on SKP1. SKP1 therefore supports a large repertoire of SCF complexes but does not possess a single meaningful “substrate specificity” of its own. (thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 4-5, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 2-4)

In a productive SCF assembly, ubiquitin is transferred through E1 and E2 enzymes to receptor-bound proteins, often generating K48-linked chains that direct the target to the 26S proteasome. The catalytic geometry can be further diversified by neddylation and, for some substrates, SCF–ARIH1 E3–E3 assemblies; SKP1’s role remains adaptor-level organization of the substrate-receptor arm.

2.2 Structural basis

NMR and biophysical analysis of recombinant human SKP1 found a predominantly monomeric protein with an approximately 19-kDa MALDI-TOF peak and sedimentation near 2.4 S. The solution structure, PDB 5XYL, contains a conserved helical core, flexible loop 1 at residues 35–49, especially mobile loop 2 at residues 67–84, a partially formed H7 helix, and a long disordered C-terminal tail. This mixture of a stable core and mobile interaction surfaces provides a plausible physical basis for accommodating many structurally distinct F-box domains. (bhattacharya2022disorderinthe pages 20-23)

This interpretation is consistent with the landmark CUL1–RBX1–SKP1–SKP2 structural model, in which SKP1 forms the bridge between the CUL1 N terminus and the F-box receptor. The important functional point is modularity: a conserved SKP1–CUL1 core can be combined with different receptors without redesigning the catalytic half of the ligase. (thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 2-4, bhattacharya2022disorderinthe pages 35-38)

3. Cellular localization

SKP1 is intracellular and has been detected in the cytoplasm, nucleus, and centrosome, fitting the locations of its many SCF partners and substrates. Affinity-purified antibody imaging detected SKP1 at interphase and mitotic centrosomes and in the interphase nucleus; biochemical purification and immunoelectron microscopy supported an authentic pericentriolar association rather than merely diffuse cytosolic staining. (freed1999componentsofan pages 1-2, freed1999componentsofan pages 2-4)

Quantitatively, approximately 97% of purified centriole doublets stained for SKP1, centrosome preparations were estimated to contain at least approximately 500 SKP1 molecules per centrosome, and SKP1 occupied a pericentriolar region extending to roughly 2 µm. Centrosomal staining resisted microtubule depolymerization, supporting association with centrosomal material rather than passive carriage on microtubules. Cellular SKP1 abundance in NIH-3T3 cells was estimated at approximately 1 µM. (freed1999componentsofan pages 2-4, freed1999componentsofan pages 4-6)

These localization experiments used mammalian mouse or hamster cells, while antibody-blocking and proteasome-perturbation assays included Xenopus systems. They therefore strongly support conserved mammalian localization but are not, by themselves, exclusively human-cell measurements. Human-cell functional studies nevertheless support relevant nuclear and centrosome-associated roles through effects on replication, micronuclei, chromosome number, and spindle/centrosome regulation. (freed1999componentsofan pages 1-2, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 6-7)

4. Principal pathways and biological processes

Cell-cycle control

Distinct SCF receptors use the SKP1-containing core to turn over cyclins, CDK regulators, phosphatases, and checkpoint proteins. Examples summarized in authoritative reviews include Cyclin D1, CDC25A, CDT1, Claspin, RRM2, and eEF2K. This timed proteolysis controls S-phase entry, replication licensing, checkpoint recovery, nucleotide supply, translation, and apoptosis. These are functions of particular SCF assemblies; SKP1 enables them but is not the substrate-recognition determinant. (thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 4-5)

Centrosome duplication and mitosis

SKP1 and CUL1 localize to centrosomes throughout the cell cycle. Anti-Skp1 or anti-Cul1 antibodies inhibited centriole separation in a cell-free system, while proteasome inhibitors blocked centriole separation and centrosome duplication in experimental embryos. More recent pathway models place SKP1-containing SCFs upstream of centrosomal proteins including CCP110, PLK4, SASS6, and BORA/AURKA, thereby coupling proteolysis to centriole number and spindle organization. (freed1999componentsofan pages 1-2, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 5-6, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 6-7)

DNA replication, repair, and chromosome stability

Human SKP1 depletion increases Cyclin E1 and produces replication stress, DNA double-strand-break markers, micronuclei, altered chromosome numbers, and chromothriptic events. Cyclin E1 correction substantially rescued these abnormalities, although incomplete rescue implies contributions from additional SCF substrates. Similar dynamic chromosome-instability phenotypes followed reduction of SKP1 or CUL1 in non-transformed fallopian-tube secretory epithelial cells over approximately three months. (thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 6-7)

Thus, the most precise interpretation is not that SKP1 constitutes a stand-alone “genome-stability pathway,” but that an adequate pool of SKP1 is required to assemble multiple SCFs whose coordinated substrate turnover prevents replication and mitotic errors.

5. Disease relevance and strength of evidence

Cancer is the best-supported disease context, but SKP1 should not be labeled simply as an oncogene or tumor suppressor. Because it is shared by tumor-suppressive and tumor-promoting SCFs, either decreased or inappropriate activity may be harmful depending on the receptor, substrate, cell state, and tissue. Reduced SKP1 can cause Cyclin E1 accumulation and chromosome instability; conversely, broadly blocking SKP1 can disrupt many essential degradation programs. (thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 1-2, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 4-5, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 6-7)

Across TCGA data summarized for 12 solid-tumor types, SKP1 mutation was rare and copy-number losses exceeded gains in 11 of 12 cancers, with shallow losses especially frequent in ovarian and prostate cancers. These observations establish recurrent alteration, not therapeutic causality. Open Targets also links SKP1 to cancer, HIV infection, neurodegenerative disease, CNS autoimmunity, and keratoconus, but such database associations aggregate heterogeneous evidence and should be treated as hypothesis-generating rather than proof of a direct disease mechanism. (OpenTargets Search: -SKP1, thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 6-7)

In a mouse model using dominant-negative Cul1-mediated Skp1 inactivation, more than 80% of animals developed T-cell lymphomas together with centrosomal and chromosomal abnormalities. This supports a causal connection between impaired SCF-core function and tumorigenesis, although it does not isolate a human SKP1-specific mechanism. (thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 5-6)

Expert reviews accordingly regard SKP1 as a plausible biomarker or therapeutic node but emphasize that causal, receptor-resolved studies are still needed before altered SKP1 abundance can be interpreted clinically. (thompson2022aberrantskp1expression pages 1-2)

6. Recent developments and applications

Direct SKP1 inhibition

Hussain et al. reported the small molecule Z0933M, which bound SKP1 with a reported K_D of 0.054 mM and engaged a hydrophobic region involving F101 and F139 near the C-terminal F-box-binding extension. The compound disrupted SKP1–F-box interactions, altered SCF-substrate handling, induced cell-cycle arrest, and produced p53-dependent cell death. The approximately 54-µM affinity and cell-based nature of the work make this a preclinical chemical probe rather than a validated drug. Published July 2022: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2022.104591. (hussain2022asmallmoleculeskp1 pages 1-2)

2024: recruiting SKP1 for targeted protein degradation

Hong et al. screened 1,284 cysteine-reactive compounds and identified EN884, an acrylamide recruiter that modifies SKP1 C160 in its flexible C-terminal region. Binding was much stronger in an assembled SKP1–FBXO7–CUL1–RBX1 complex than against isolated SKP1, showing that protein context and conformation matter. Cellular chemoproteomics measured approximately 7% C160 engagement, while a clickable derivative enriched SKP1 2.8-fold. Published February 16, 2024: https://doi.org/10.1021/acschembio.3c00642. (hong2024exploitingthecullin pages 11-13, hong2024exploitingthecullin pages 1-2, hong2024exploitingthecullin pages 2-4)

Linking the recruiter to JQ1 produced BRD4-directed degraders. The lead compound caused 94% BRD4 loss after 24 hours, compared with 42% for a non-reactive analog. Degradation was blocked by SKP1 knockdown and attenuated by the proteasome inhibitor bortezomib and the neddylation inhibitor MLN4924, supporting dependence on SKP1, the proteasome, and an active Cullin–RING system. Related molecules degraded androgen receptor in LNCaP prostate-cancer cells in a proteasome-dependent manner. (hong2024exploitingthecullin pages 6-8, hong2024exploitingthecullin pages 4-6, hong2024exploitingthecullin pages 13-19)

This work provides proof of concept that an essential core adaptor—not only a conventional substrate receptor—can be exploited for targeted degradation. However, EN884 derivatives displayed off-target activity, early-hit potency/selectivity limitations, and evidence of reversible recruitment by nominally non-reactive analogs. Complete AR dependency testing was complicated because SKP1 knockdown was lethal and MLN4924 itself reduced AR. No clinical implementation has yet been established. (hong2024exploitingthecullin pages 6-8, hong2024exploitingthecullin pages 4-6)

7. Evidence matrix

The following table summarizes the strongest identity, mechanistic, localization, phenotype, and application evidence.

Topic Best-supported finding Evidence type / key quantitative detail Source / date / DOI
Identity and aliases The research target is human SKP1, the S-phase kinase-associated protein 1 specified as UniProt P63208. Literature describes a 163-aa prototypic protein and historical aliases p19, OCP2, and TCEB1L; the gene maps to 5q31.1. Protein annotation supplied for P63208 agrees with literature on human SKP1 identity, size, aliases, and SCF-complex function. A shorter 160-aa splice isoform has also been reported. Thompson et al., March 2022, https://doi.org/10.3389/fcell.2022.859582; Hussain et al., July 2022, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2022.104591
Primary function and distinction from SKP2 SKP1 is a non-catalytic adaptor/scaffold in SCF ubiquitin ligases. Its N-terminal region binds CUL1, while its C-terminal region binds the F-box domain of a substrate receptor. SKP2 is one such F-box substrate receptor—not SKP1 and not a synonym for it. Mechanistic and structural evidence assigns ubiquitin-transfer machinery to RBX1/E2 and substrate selection to the variable F-box protein. SKP1 physically couples these modules and has no demonstrated catalytic reaction or intrinsic substrate specificity. Approximately 69 mammalian F-box proteins can potentially diversify SCF complexes. Zheng et al., April 2002, https://doi.org/10.1038/416703a; Thompson et al., March 2022, https://doi.org/10.3389/fcell.2022.859582
Structure and domains The literature agrees with the supplied SKP1-family, SKP1-like, dimerization-superfamily, and BTB/POZ-superfamily annotations. SKP1 has a conserved helical core and N-terminal BTB/POZ-like CUL1-binding region, plus a structurally adaptable C-terminal F-box-binding extension. NMR of predominantly monomeric human SKP1 produced PDB 5XYL and identified flexible loop 1 (residues 35–49), especially flexible loop 2 (67–84), a partially formed helix H7, and a long disordered C-terminal tail. Sedimentation remained near 2.4 S, and MALDI-TOF showed a major approximately 19-kDa species. Bhattacharya et al., November 2022, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmb.2022.167830
Cellular localization SKP1 operates principally as an intracellular protein in the cytoplasm, nucleus, and centrosome, consistent with SCF-dependent control of soluble, nuclear, and centrosomal substrates. Centrosomal SKP1 persists through interphase and mitosis. Immunofluorescence, purified-centrosome biochemistry, deconvolution microscopy, and immunoelectron microscopy detected SKP1 around and between centrioles. About 97% of purified centriole doublets stained positive; preparations contained at least approximately 500 SKP1 molecules per centrosome, and cellular abundance in NIH-3T3 cells was estimated at approximately 1 μM. Some localization evidence used mouse or hamster cells and Xenopus functional assays rather than human cells. Freed et al., September 1999, https://doi.org/10.1101/gad.13.17.2242
Pathways and genome stability By enabling different SCF complexes, SKP1 supports timed degradation of regulators of cell-cycle transitions, DNA replication and repair, apoptosis, centrosome duplication, spindle formation, and chromosome segregation. Reduced SKP1 can stabilize Cyclin E1 and provoke chromosome instability. Human-cell silencing increased nuclear area, micronuclei, abnormal chromosome numbers, replication stress, DNA double-strand breaks, and chromothriptic events. Cyclin E1 rescue experiments explained much—but not all—of the phenotype. In TCGA analyses summarized across 12 solid-tumor types, SKP1 losses exceeded gains in 11 of 12, although mutations were rare. Thompson et al., February 2020, https://doi.org/10.3390/cancers12030531; Thompson et al., March 2022, https://doi.org/10.3389/fcell.2022.859582
Experimental inhibitor Z0933M Z0933M was reported as a direct small-molecule SKP1 inhibitor/modulator that interferes with SKP1–F-box interactions, disrupts SCF function, and induces cell-cycle arrest and p53-dependent cell death. Reported binding affinity KD = 0.054 mM. Binding was mapped near a C-terminal hydrophobic hotspot involving F101 and F139. Evidence is preclinical; potency is modest and no clinical efficacy was established. Hussain et al., July 2022, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2022.104591
EN884 and SKP1-based targeted degradation EN884 is an acrylamide-containing recruiter that engages SKP1 C160 preferentially in an assembled SCF complex. EN884-derived heterobifunctional degraders redirected the machinery toward neo-substrates BRD4 and androgen receptor. EN884 emerged from a 1,284-compound cysteine-reactive screen. Cellular engagement of C160 was reported at 7%, and a clickable probe enriched SKP1 2.8-fold. The lead BRD4 degrader caused 94% loss at 24 h versus 42% for a non-reactive analog; activity was blocked by SKP1 knockdown and attenuated by bortezomib and MLN4924. AR degradation in LNCaP cells was proteasome-dependent. Hong et al., February 16, 2024, https://doi.org/10.1021/acschembio.3c00642
Evidence limitations The core adaptor assignment is well supported, but many downstream phenotypes reflect entire SCF complexes and cannot be attributed to a unique SKP1 substrate. Direct SKP1 drug discovery remains preclinical, and broad inhibition may be toxic because SKP1 is shared by many essential SCF ligases. Human-specific localization data are less complete than mammalian/Xenopus evidence. Z0933M has millimolar-to-high-micromolar affinity. EN884 shows off-target labeling and early-hit potency/selectivity limitations; non-reactive analogs also retained degradation activity, and complete SKP1-dependency testing for AR was impeded by lethality of SKP1 knockdown. Disease associations are therefore mechanistically plausible but not equivalent to clinical validation. Thompson et al., March 2022, https://doi.org/10.3389/fcell.2022.859582; Hussain et al., July 2022, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2022.104591; Hong et al., February 2024, https://doi.org/10.1021/acschembio.3c00642

Table: Concise evidence matrix verifying human SKP1 identity and summarizing its non-catalytic SCF-adaptor mechanism, structure, localization, phenotypes, and emerging chemical applications. The final row highlights important organismal, mechanistic, and translational limitations.

8. Overall functional annotation

Recommended primary annotation: Human SKP1/P63208 is a conserved, non-catalytic intracellular adaptor of CUL1-based SCF E3 ubiquitin ligases. Its N-terminal SKP1/BTB-like region associates with CUL1, while its structurally adaptable C-terminal region binds the F-box domain of interchangeable substrate receptors. It thereby positions receptor-bound targets near the RBX1/E2 ubiquitin-transfer machinery for ubiquitination and, commonly, proteasomal degradation.

Primary operating locations: cytoplasm, nucleus, and centrosomes; the exact distribution is partner- and cell-state-dependent.

Most directly supported biological roles: assembly of SCF complexes controlling cell-cycle transitions, replication and DNA-damage responses, centrosome duplication, mitotic-spindle integrity, chromosome segregation, and apoptosis.

Confidence assessment: High confidence for protein identity, family/domain consistency, SCF-adaptor mechanism, and lack of intrinsic catalytic activity; moderate-to-high confidence for conserved mammalian nuclear/cytoplasmic/centrosomal localization; moderate confidence for disease-specific interpretation because many phenotypes reflect disruption of the whole SCF repertoire. Direct pharmacological targeting and SKP1-recruited degradation are promising but remain preclinical.

📚 Additional Documentation

Notes

(SKP1-notes.md)

SKP1 (human, UniProt P63208) — curation notes

Working journal for the GO annotation review in SKP1-ai-review.yaml. Sources: SKP1-uniprot.txt,
SKP1-goa.tsv, SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md, cached publications in publications/, cached
Reactome reactions in reactome/, and the cached GO-CAM models listed in gocams/index.tsv.

1. Identity, and the one thing to keep straight

P63208 is SKP1, the small adaptor subunit of SCF ligases — not SKP2, which is one of the ~69
F-box substrate receptors that dock onto it. The deep-research report flags this explicitly, and it
matters because a large fraction of the GOA rows cite papers whose titles name a receptor
(SKP2, FBXW7, beta-TrCP, cyclin F, FBXO7…) rather than SKP1
[file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md "SKP1 is not SKP2. SKP2 is an F-box substrate receptor that binds SKP1 in the SCF^SKP2 complex"].
Aliases in the record: p19skp1, OCP2/OCP-II (organ of Corti protein 2), TCEB1L, SKP1A.

2. What SKP1 actually does

Two contacts, no chemistry:

  • N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region → the first cullin repeat at the CUL1 N-terminus.
  • Adaptable C-terminal helices → the ~40-residue F-box motif of a substrate receptor.

[file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md "Human SKP1 contains an N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region participating in CUL1 association and a helical, conformationally adaptable C-terminal region that binds F-box domains."]
[file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt "In the SCF complex, serves as an adapter that links the F-box protein to CUL1."]

The SCF crystal structure is the anchor: CUL1's stalk "binds the Skp1-F boxSkp2 protein
substrate-recognition complex at its tip"
PMID:11961546,
and the beta-TrCP1-SKP1-beta-catenin structure shows the substrate being read by the receptor's
WD40 domain
PMID:12820959.

SKP1 is catalytically inert and has no substrate specificity of its own
[file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md "SKP1 provides structural connectivity rather than catalytic chemistry. It has no established intrinsic enzymatic reaction, catalytic substrate, or transporter function."]
[file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md "SKP1 therefore supports a large repertoire of SCF complexes but does not possess a single meaningful “substrate specificity” of its own."].
Its flexibility is what lets one adaptor accept structurally diverse F-box domains (NMR, PDB 5XYL;
mobile loop 1 35–49, loop 2 67–84, partly formed H7, disordered C-tail)
[file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md "This mixture of a stable core and mobile interaction surfaces provides a plausible physical basis for accommodating many structurally distinct F-box domains."].

Beyond canonical SCF, SKP1 sits in:

  • CRL7(FBXW8) — SKP1-FBXW8 docks onto CUL7 and links it to a neddylated CUL1-RBX1 catalytic module
    PMID:35982156.
  • CUL1-RING(FBXL4), mitochondrial, degrading BNIP3/BNIP3L
    [file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt "Also acts as a core component of the Cul1- RING(FBXL4) ubiquitin ligase complex, which mediates the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of BNIP3 and BNI3L"].
  • MYCBP2/PAM-FBXO45-SKP1, with no cullin at all, where SKP1 does more than scaffold
    PMID:29997255
    PMID:29997255.
  • PRC1.1 / BCOR variant Polycomb complexes, via the F-box/JmjC protein KDM2B/FBXL10
    [file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt "The KDM2B-SKP1 heterodimeric complex interacts with the PCGF1-BCORL heterodimeric complex to form a homotetrameric polycomb repression complex 1 (PRC1.1)"]
    PMID:16943429.

A genuinely non-degradative activity, which I treated as a third core function: the nuclear
export signal of FBXO7 lies inside its F-box, so SKP1 and CRM1 compete for the same surface
PMID:21378169
PMID:21378169
PMID:21378169.
More than ten other F-box proteins share this NES placement, so it is not a one-receptor quirk, and
SKP1 itself is the entity doing the occluding — participation, not mere necessity.

3. Localization

Nucleus/nucleoplasm, cytosol/cytoplasm, chromatin (via PRC1.1) and centrosome
[file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md "SKP1 is intracellular and has been detected in the cytoplasm, nucleus, and centrosome, fitting the locations of its many SCF partners and substrates."].
The centrosome data are strong quantitatively
[file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md "approximately 97% of purified centriole doublets stained for SKP1, centrosome preparations were estimated to contain at least approximately 500 SKP1 molecules per centrosome"]
[file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md "Anti-Skp1 or anti-Cul1 antibodies inhibited centriole separation in a cell-free system"],
but the targeting is receptor-driven (cyclin F, FBXW5, FBXL13), so I kept centrosome non-core,
matching how RBX1 was handled on the same reference (PMID:20596027).

4. Decisions and why

The 265 bare GO:0005515 IPI rows (already adjudicated before I picked this up; I spot-checked a
sample and left them intact). Repository policy: resolve to an informative MF where the evidence
supports one, otherwise REMOVE as uninformative without asserting the interaction is false. The
prior reviewer's split is consistent — F-box partners from focused SCF-assembly/substrate studies
→ MODIFY to GO:1990444 + GO:0160072; CUL1 → GO:0097602; high-throughput interactome hits
(BioPlex 3.0, HuRI, HI-II-14, PcG complexome) → REMOVE. All 195 REMOVEs in the file are
GO:0005515 rows, and each carries the "removal records that the generic term is uninformative,
not that the interaction is false" wording.

Core MF: GO:0160072, not GO:1990756. SKP1 carries three overlapping MF rows from the same
beta-TrCP1-SKP1-beta-catenin structure: scaffold activity (GO:0160072), ligase-substrate adaptor
activity (GO:1990756) and ligase activator activity (GO:1990757). The term definitions separate
cleanly: GO:1990756 is "brings together a ubiquitin-like ligase and its substrate", which is what
the F-box protein does (SKP2 and BTRC both carry it — see genes/human/SKP2), while GO:0160072 is
"brings together an ubiquitin ligase and an ubiquitin ligase-substrate adaptor", which is exactly
SKP1's position. So I ACCEPTed GO:0160072 and MODIFY'd both GO:1990756 and GO:1990757 to it. The
"activator" framing does fit the cullin-less PAM/FBXO45 case, and that is separately and correctly
annotated as GO:0140677 — which the GO-CAM model gomodel:63c0ac2b00000506 also uses for the SKP1
node, so I ACCEPTed it rather than folding it into the scaffold term.

GO:0008013 beta-catenin binding (IDA) → MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED. SKP1 is in a ternary complex with
beta-catenin, but the specific contact is beta-TrCP1's WD40 domain reading the DpSGphiXpS degron.
Not REMOVE: the curator saw a real structure containing both proteins, and SKP1's informative
functions (GO:1990444, GO:0160072) are already annotated.

GO:0019904 protein domain specific binding (IPI, with mouse Cacybp/SIP Q9CXW3) → MODIFY to
GO:0160072. Verified the partner via UniProt REST: Q9CXW3 = mouse Cacybp (calcyclin-binding
protein = SIP). The paper maps the contact to SIP's CS domain
PMID:15996101
and describes SKP1 doing its usual job in a non-cullin assembly
PMID:15996101.

Ortholog-transfer rows (GO:0000775 centromeric region, GO:0007129 meiotic pairing) →
KEEP_AS_NON_CORE, not REMOVE. Checked the source via QuickGO: mouse Skp1 (Q9WTX5) carries
GO:0000775 by IDA and GO:0007129 by IMP, both from PMID:39244596, a mouse meiosis study.
These are real experimental annotations on a near-identical ortholog, so the transfer is not mine to
overrule; but a germline/stage-restricted context is not the core adaptor function. Same logic for
GO:0005813 centrosome IEA (mouse IDA source, PMID:10485847).

IBA rows (GO:0005634, GO:0005737, GO:0031146, GO:0097602) → ACCEPT. All sit at
PANTHER:PTN000126179 with descendants across fly, mouse, fission yeast, budding yeast, Dictyostelium
and Arabidopsis. Human P63208 appears in its own WITH/FROM on three of them — that is the marker
that experimental grounding exists on the target itself, and is explicitly not to be called
circular. No target-specific evidence of loss or divergence exists for SKP1, so the node placement
stands.

Receptor-driven process rows. The recurring judgement on this gene: does the process belong to
the adaptor or to whichever F-box protein it is carrying? Kept as non-core where the
SKP1-containing ligase demonstrably acts (iron homeostasis via FBXL5; circadian period via
FBXL3/FBXL21; TOR signalling via FBXO9; BMP via FBXL15; inflammation via FBXO3; xenophagy via FBXO2 —
where SKP1 was explicitly shown to be required
PMID:34515398;
mitophagy via the FBXL4 ligase of which SKP1 is a core subunit per UniProt; centrosome duplication
regulation; DNA-damage checkpoint via FBX4; NMJ/synapse assembly via the MYCBP2-FBXO45-SKP1 module).
Marked over-annotated where the claim is a distal organismal phenotype of one receptor or where
the executing entity is plainly another subunit: limb development (mouse dactylin/FBXW4), neural
crest differentiation (FBXL17), regulation of apoptosis (FBXL18→FBXL7), generic regulation of
DNA-templated transcription and negative regulation of transcription, and heterochromatin formation
(done by the Polycomb catalytic/reader subunits, not by SKP1). This grading mirrors CUL1 and RBX1 on
the identical NAS references.

Two MODIFYs for altitude, both matching the correction already applied to CUL1:
- GO:0051298 centrosome duplication → GO:0010824 regulation of centrosome duplication. The SCF
ligases restrain and time duplication (SCF(FBXW5)→SAS-6, SCF(cyclin F)→CP110); they do not perform
it. Note the cited reference (PMID:34388369) is the human signal peptidase complex structure
and does not address centrosomes at all, so it cannot carry the direct term either.
- GO:0060271 cilium assembly → GO:1902017 regulation of cilium assembly. SCF(FBXW5) removes the
depolymerase MCAK whose excess blocks ciliogenesis
PMID:34368969.

GO:0000151 ubiquitin ligase complex → ACCEPT (not MODIFY to GO:0019005). The general parent is
the right level here precisely because SKP1 is not confined to SCF: CRL7(FBXW8) and the
cullin-less PAM/FBXO45 ligase would both fall outside GO:0019005.

Reactome TAS rows (22 nucleoplasm + 46 cytosol) → ACCEPT, each summarised with its own reaction
name, as done for CUL1. Every reaction is a curated SCF step in the stated compartment.

5. proposed_new_terms: [] — and the comparator check behind it

Tempting candidates and why each was rejected:

  • Protein complex assembly / ubiquitin ligase complex assembly. SKP1 is a constitutive subunit
    of the complexes in question, not an assembly factor acting on them from outside; the assembly-factor
    role in this pathway belongs to CAND1, which exchanges receptors, and to SGT1/HSP90. Comparator
    check: CUL1 and RBX1 — the other two invariant SCF subunits, in the same structural role — carry no
    such term in human, mouse or rat. A systematic absence across three MODs is a convention, not a gap.
  • Positive regulation of ubiquitin-protein transferase activity. This is the "activator" framing
    again; GO:0140677 already covers the one case where an enhancement was actually measured
    (FBXO45-NMNAT2), and extending it to SCF generally would assert an allosteric role the structures
    do not show.
  • Centriole separation / chromosome stability process terms. SKP1 depletion does cause replication
    stress, micronuclei and chromothripsis
    [file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md "Human SKP1 depletion increases Cyclin E1 and produces replication stress, DNA double-strand-break markers, micronuclei, altered chromosome numbers, and chromothriptic events."],
    but this is necessity evidence for assembling the whole SCF repertoire, not participation in a
    distinct process — as the deep-research report itself concludes
    [file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md "the most precise interpretation is not that SKP1 constitutes a stand-alone “genome-stability pathway,” but that an adequate pool of SKP1 is required to assemble multiple SCFs whose coordinated substrate turnover prevents replication and mitotic errors."]
    Existing GO:0031146 / GO:0043161 / GO:0000082 already express what SKP1 contributes.

6. Consistency with partners and models

  • Grading kept in line with the completed reviews of the other SCF subunits: genes/human/CUL1
    (scaffold, GO:0160072 core), genes/human/RBX1 (catalysis, GO:0061630 core), genes/human/SKP2
    (substrate recognition, GO:1990756 core). SKP1 takes GO:0160072 as its core MF with
    contributes_to GO:0061630 — it has no catalytic activity of its own.
  • modules/g1_s_transition.yaml cites SKP1 (UniProtKB:P63208) as the SCF adaptor exemplar; consistent.
  • GO-CAM models containing SKP1 (gocams/index.tsv): FBXO9/CARM1, FBXO7/SIRT7, cyclin F/CP110,
    cyclin F/EXO1, cyclin F/RRM2, FBXO28/RAB27A all type the SKP1 node as GO:0160072, and the
    PAM/FBXO45/NMNAT2 model (gomodel:63c0ac2b00000506) types it as GO:0140677. Both terms are
    ACCEPTed here, so the review and the models agree.

7. Outcome

Status COMPLETE; 443/443 annotations reviewed. Actions: 195 REMOVE (all bare GO:0005515),
139 ACCEPT, 75 MODIFY, 27 KEEP_AS_NON_CORE, 7 MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED. Three core functions
(SCF adaptor/scaffold; substrate-receptor-module partner in cullin-less and CRL7 ligases; nuclear
retention of F-box proteins). just validate human SKP1 passes with no errors and no warnings.

taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:9606
  label: Homo sapiens
description: 'SKP1 (S-phase kinase-associated protein 1, p19skp1) is the small, highly conserved adaptor subunit of SCF
  (SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein) cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligases, the largest family of E3s in human cells. It is a 163-residue
  protein with an N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region that binds the first cullin repeat at the N-terminus of CUL1, and a helical,
  conformationally adaptable C-terminal region - with two mobile loops and a partly formed final helix - that clamps the
  ~40-residue F-box motif. Through that pair of contacts SKP1 tethers any one of the roughly 69 human F-box substrate receptors
  (SKP2, BTRC/FBXW11 beta-TrCP, FBXW7, cyclin F/CCNF, FBXL3, FBXL5, FBXO7, FBXO9, FBXO31 and others) to the CUL1-RBX1 catalytic
  core, where RBX1 recruits a ubiquitin-charged E2 (CDC34/UBE2R, UBE2D). SKP1 has no catalytic activity and forms no ubiquitin
  thioester: it contributes the geometry that brings a receptor-bound substrate within reach of the E2, and substrate choice
  rests entirely with the F-box protein. The assembled ligases build mainly K48-linked chains that commit substrates to
  the 26S proteasome - Thr187-phosphorylated p27/CDKN1B via SCF(SKP2) at the G1/S transition, IkappaB-alpha, beta-catenin,
  EMI1, CDC25A and NFE2L2 via SCF(beta-TrCP), cyclin E, MYC, NOTCH and WDR5 via SCF(FBXW7), CP110 and E2F1 via SCF(cyclin
  F), the cryptochromes via SCF(FBXL3)/SCF(FBXL21), and IRP2 via SCF(FBXL5). The same adaptor serves ligases built on other
  scaffolds and, in some cases, without a cullin at all: it is a core subunit of the CRL7(FBXW8) assembly and of the mitochondrial
  CUL1-RING(FBXL4) ligase, and in the CUL1-independent MYCBP2/PAM-FBXO45-SKP1 ligase it goes beyond scaffolding to strengthen
  the receptor''s grip on its substrate NMNAT2. Independently of ubiquitination, SKP1 binding masks nuclear export signals
  that lie within the F-box of FBXO7 and a sixth of other F-box proteins, retaining them in the nucleus. SKP1 acts in the
  nucleus and nucleoplasm, in the cytosol, on chromatin as part of the KDM2B-SKP1 module of PRC1.1 variant Polycomb complexes,
  and at centrosomes, where it is present on nearly all purified centriole doublets. Because an adequate pool of SKP1 is
  needed to assemble the whole SCF repertoire, its depletion stabilises cyclin E1 and produces replication stress, micronuclei
  and chromosome instability.'

- term:
    id: GO:0000775
    label: chromosome, centromeric region
  evidence_type: ISS
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000024
  qualifier: located_in
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9WTX5
  review:
    summary: Ortholog transfer from mouse Skp1 (UniProtKB:Q9WTX5), which carries an IDA annotation to the centromeric chromosome
      region from a meiotic study; no human-cell evidence supports this location directly.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The source is a mouse experimental annotation, transferred by curator judgment of sequence similarity, and the
      orthologs are essentially identical, so the transfer is sound and should not be overruled. But a meiotic centromeric
      pool is a stage-restricted context rather than part of the core adaptor function, so it is kept as non-core.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
      supporting_text: SKP1 is intracellular and has been detected in the **cytoplasm, nucleus, and centrosome**, fitting
        the locations of its many SCF partners and substrates.
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: In oocytes and preimplantation embryos, SCF ubiquitin ligase complexes are maintained inactive by
        cytoplasmic lattices.
- term:
    id: GO:0000785
    label: chromatin
  evidence_type: NAS
  original_reference_id: PMID:22325352
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: Chromatin association of SKP1 via the KDM2B-SKP1 module of PRC1.1, which is recruited to CpG islands and BCL6
      target genes.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: A legitimate location for the PRC1.1-bound pool of SKP1, but one that follows from the KDM2B partnership rather
      than from the SCF adaptor activity; nucleus, nucleoplasm and cytosol are the core locations. Kept as non-core.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: The KDM2B-SKP1 heterodimeric complex interacts with the PCGF1-BCORL heterodimeric complex to form
        a homotetrameric polycomb repression complex 1 (PRC1.1)
    - reference_id: PMID:16943429
      supporting_text: the BCOR complex contains components of a second ubiquitin E3 ligase, namely, SKP1 and FBXL10 (JHDM1B)
    - reference_id: PMID:22325352
      supporting_text: we present a comprehensive proteomic and genomic analysis that uncovered six major groups of PRC1
        complexes, each containing a distinct PCGF subunit, a RING1A/B ubiquitin ligase, and a unique set of associated
        polypeptides
- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:11238952
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9UKT8
  review:
    summary: SKP1 binds FBXW2, the WD40 receptor for GCM1 and SKP2 (FBXW2) through the ~40-residue F-box motif, forming
      the SKP1-FBXW2 substrate-receptor module; evidence from SCF(beta-TrCP)-dependent ATF4 degradation, with FBXW2 assayed
      alongside beta-TrCP.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The informative molecular function behind this interaction is F-box domain binding (GO:1990444): the C-terminal
      helices of SKP1 dock the F-box motif of the receptor, which is how SKP1 tethers FBXW2 to CUL1-RBX1 (ubiquitin ligase
      complex scaffold activity, GO:0160072). Bare protein binding does not capture this.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:1990444
      label: F-box domain binding
    - id: GO:0160072
      label: ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:11238952
      supporting_text: Here we show that the F-box protein betaTrCP, the receptor component of the SCF E3 ubiquitin ligase
        responsible for IkappaBalpha and beta-catenin degradation, is colocalized in the nucleus with ATF4, a member of
        the ATF-CREB bZIP family of transcription factors, and controls its stability.
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: In the SCF complex, serves as an adapter that links the F-box protein to CUL1.
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
      supporting_text: Human SKP1 contains an N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region participating in CUL1 association and a helical,
        conformationally adaptable C-terminal region that binds F-box domains.

  review:
    summary: SKP1 binds CUL1, the cullin scaffold whose N-terminal cullin repeat carries the SKP1-F-box module; evidence
      from the CAND1 study, in which CAND1 occupies unneddylated CUL1 and blocks SKP1/SKP2 binding.

      supporting_text: Human SKP1 contains an N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region participating in CUL1 association and a helical,
        conformationally adaptable C-terminal region that binds F-box domains.

  original_reference_id: PMID:26085330
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:O94952
  review:
    summary: SKP1 binds FBXO21, the receptor for EID1 (FBXO21) through the ~40-residue F-box motif, forming the SKP1-FBXO21
      substrate-receptor module; evidence from the FBXO21/EID1 study.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The informative molecular function behind this interaction is F-box domain binding (GO:1990444): the C-terminal
      helices of SKP1 dock the F-box motif of the receptor, which is how SKP1 tethers FBXO21 to CUL1-RBX1 (ubiquitin ligase
      complex scaffold activity, GO:0160072). Bare protein binding does not capture this.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:1990444
      label: F-box domain binding
    - id: GO:0160072
      label: ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:26085330
      supporting_text: We have now applied this approach to an uncharacterized human F-box protein, FBXO21, which serves
        as the substrate-recognition subunit of a SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein (SCF)-type E3, thereby identifying EID1 (EP300-interacting
        inhibitor of differentiation 1) as a candidate substrate.
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: In the SCF complex, serves as an adapter that links the F-box protein to CUL1.
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
      supporting_text: Human SKP1 contains an N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region participating in CUL1 association and a helical,
        conformationally adaptable C-terminal region that binds F-box domains.

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:33692209
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q8NHM5
  review:
    summary: SKP1 binds KDM2B/FBXL10, an F-box histone demethylase and PRC1.1 subunit (KDM2B) through the ~40-residue F-box
      motif, forming the SKP1-KDM2B substrate-receptor module; evidence from the KDM2B/KSHV study showing KDM2B binds the
      SCF complex via its F-box.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The informative molecular function behind this interaction is F-box domain binding (GO:1990444): the C-terminal
      helices of SKP1 dock the F-box motif of the receptor, which is how SKP1 tethers KDM2B to CUL1-RBX1 (ubiquitin ligase
      complex scaffold activity, GO:0160072). Bare protein binding does not capture this.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:1990444
      label: F-box domain binding
    - id: GO:0160072
      label: ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:33692209
      supporting_text: This effect is dependent upon the binding of KDM2B to the SKP1-CUL1-F-box (SCF) E3 ubiquitin ligase
        complex via its F-box domain.
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: In the SCF complex, serves as an adapter that links the F-box protein to CUL1.
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
      supporting_text: Human SKP1 contains an N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region participating in CUL1 association and a helical,
        conformationally adaptable C-terminal region that binds F-box domains.

    summary: 'Centrosomal pool of SKP1: SKP1 and CUL1 were detected on interphase and mitotic centrosomes, with SKP1 on
      ~97% of purified centriole doublets, and SCF(cyclin F) acts on CP110 at centrioles in G2. Ortholog transfer from mouse

  review:

    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt

        cytoplasmic lattices.
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
      supporting_text: the most precise interpretation is not that SKP1 constitutes a stand-alone “genome-stability pathway,”
        but that an adequate pool of SKP1 is required to assemble multiple SCFs whose coordinated substrate turnover prevents
        replication and mitotic errors.

      motif of beta-catenin is read by the WD40 domain of beta-TrCP1, while SKP1 binds the F-box of beta-TrCP1.
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: Not wrong that SKP1 is in a complex containing beta-catenin, but the direct, specific contact with the substrate
      is made by the receptor, not by SKP1, so annotating beta-catenin binding to the adaptor over-reads the structure.
      SKP1 substrate contacts in general are indirect - the informative functions are F-box domain binding (GO:1990444)
      and scaffold activity (GO:0160072), both already annotated.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:12820959
      supporting_text: The 3.0 A structure of a beta-TrCP1-Skp1-beta-catenin complex reveals the basis of substrate recognition
        by the beta-TrCP1 WD40 domain
    - reference_id: PMID:12820959
      supporting_text: SCFs bind substrates through the interchangeable F box protein subunit, with the >70 human F box
        proteins allowing the recognition of a wide range of substrates
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
      supporting_text: These are functions of particular SCF assemblies; SKP1 enables them but is not the substrate-recognition
        determinant.
- term:
    id: GO:0010564
    label: regulation of cell cycle process
  evidence_type: NAS
  original_reference_id: PMID:31424118
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: SKP1 is the adaptor of the ligases through which SCF(cyclin F) degrades E2F1, which underlies the synthetic
      lethality between cyclin F loss and CHK1 inhibition.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: 'Genuine but receptor-specific: the outcome is determined by the F-box protein that SKP1 happens to carry, not
      by SKP1 itself, and SKP1 supports ligases with opposite-sign outputs through different receptors. Retained as a non-core
      process rather than removed, because the SKP1-containing ligase really does act here. The specific cell-cycle claims
      worth keeping on SKP1 are the G1/S transition and SCF-dependent proteolysis terms; this generic regulatory term is
      retained as non-core rather than removed.'
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:31424118
      supporting_text: cyclin F does not partner with a CDK, but instead forms via its F-box domain an SCF (Skp1-Cul1-F-box)-type
        E3 ubiquitin ligase module
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
      supporting_text: the most precise interpretation is not that SKP1 constitutes a stand-alone “genome-stability pathway,”
        but that an adequate pool of SKP1 is required to assemble multiple SCFs whose coordinated substrate turnover prevents
        replication and mitotic errors.

  - FB:FBgn0025637

  - PANTHER:PTN000126179
  - PomBase:SPBC409.05

  - UniProtKB:P63208
  review:
    summary: SKP1 is required for, and forms part of, the SCF ligases that ubiquitinate receptor-selected substrates for
      proteasomal degradation. Inferred at the SKP1-family ancestral node PANTHER:PTN000126179 from experimentally annotated
      descendants in fly, mouse, fission yeast, budding yeast and human.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: 'Core process: every SCF ligase that SKP1 serves ends in proteasomal destruction of a receptor-selected substrate,
      and SKP1 performs part of the work of that process - it holds the receptor, and therefore the substrate, in register
      with the RBX1-bound E2. The claim is about the shared core subunit rather than any one receptor, which is exactly
      the level at which this term sits. The PAINT curator placed this assertion at the ancestral node PANTHER:PTN000126179
      after reading the experimental annotations of the extant SKP1 family, and human P63208 appears among the descendant
      evidences precisely because it carries direct experimental support - that is expected, not circular.'
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: Essential component of the SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein) ubiquitin ligase complex, which mediates
        the ubiquitination of proteins involved in cell cycle progression, signal transduction and transcription.
    - reference_id: file:human/SKP1/SKP1-deep-research-falcon.md
      supporting_text: ubiquitin is transferred through E1 and E2 enzymes to receptor-bound proteins, often generating K48-linked
        chains that direct the target to the 26S proteasome

  review:
    summary: Derived from the PRC1-family proteomics work, via SKP1 membership of the PRC1.1 variant complex.
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: Heterochromatin formation is an activity of the Polycomb catalytic and reader subunits; SKP1 contributes only
      the F-box contact that recruits KDM2B into that complex, and the cited paper characterises the PRC1 groups without

        complexes, each containing a distinct PCGF subunit, a RING1A/B ubiquitin ligase, and a unique set of associated

- term:
    id: GO:0051457
    label: maintenance of protein location in nucleus
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:21378169
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9Y3I1
  review:
    summary: The nuclear export signal of FBXO7 (UniProtKB:Q9Y3I1) lies inside its F-box, so SKP1 binding and CRM1 binding
      are mutually exclusive; SKP1 occupancy blocks CRM1 and lets FBXO7 accumulate in the nucleus from the G1/S transition.
      More than ten other F-box proteins share this NES placement.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: 'Genuine participation, and by SKP1 itself rather than by a receptor: SKP1 is the entity that occludes the export
      signal, so the retention is its own activity and not a downstream outcome of ubiquitination. It is demonstrated directly
      in human cells, applies to roughly a sixth of F-box proteins rather than to one receptor, and follows from the same
      F-box contact that defines the protein - hence retained as a core, non-degradative output of the adaptor function.'
    supported_by:

      supporting_text: Skp1 binding prevented Fbxo7 from contacting CRM1
    - reference_id: PMID:21378169

        to form part of an E3 ubiquitin ligase
    - reference_id: PMID:21378169
      supporting_text: We propose that this competitive binding allowed Fbxo7 to accumulate within the nucleus starting
        at the G1/S transition

  review:
    summary: Annotated from the beta-TrCP1-SKP1-beta-catenin structure. In that assembly the substrate is held by the WD40
      domain of beta-TrCP1; SKP1 holds the receptor, not the substrate.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: The term definition requires bringing a ubiquitin-like ligase together with its substrate, and that is what
      the F-box protein does (SKP2 and BTRC carry this term). SKP1 sits one step further out, joining the ligase core to
      the substrate adaptor, which is ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity (GO:0160072) - already annotated to SKP1
      by IDA. Keeping both blurs the division of labour that the two terms exist to express.

      label: ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
    supported_by:

        by the beta-TrCP1 WD40 domain

core_functions:
- description: 'Adaptor of SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box-RBX1) cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases: the N-terminal BTB/POZ-like region
    binds the CUL1 N-terminal cullin repeat while the adaptable C-terminal helices clamp the F-box motif of one of ~69 interchangeable
    substrate receptors, holding the receptor-bound substrate in register with the ubiquitin-charged E2 delivered by RBX1.
    SKP1 performs no chemistry itself; it supplies the connection and the geometry through which mainly K48-linked chains
    are built on receptor-selected substrates, such as Thr187-phosphorylated p27/CDKN1B via SCF(SKP2) at the G1/S transition.'
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0160072
    label: ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
  contributes_to_molecular_function:
    id: GO:0061630
    label: ubiquitin protein ligase activity
  directly_involved_in:

    CUL1-independent MYCBP2/PAM-FBXO45-SKP1 ligase SKP1 acts as an auxiliary component of the target-recognition module,
    strengthening FBXO45 binding to NMNAT2 so that the ligase polyubiquitinates it, and in CRL7 the SKP1-FBXW8 pair docks
    onto CUL7 and links it to a neddylated CUL1-RBX1 catalytic module.'

- description: 'Nuclear retention of F-box proteins through the same F-box contact: because the leucine-rich nuclear export
    signal of FBXO7 and of more than ten other F-box proteins is embedded in the F-box domain, SKP1 binding physically occludes
    it and prevents exportin 1/CRM1 engagement, so the receptor accumulates in the nucleus from the G1/S transition onwards.
    SKP1 occupancy therefore sets where a subset of SCF ligases can assemble and act.'

      to form part of an E3 ubiquitin ligase
  - reference_id: PMID:21378169
    supporting_text: We propose that this competitive binding allowed Fbxo7 to accumulate within the nucleus starting at
      the G1/S transition

suggested_questions:
- question: Should the ~265 GO:0005515 rows recording SKP1 with individual F-box proteins be re-curated as F-box domain
    binding (GO:1990444) plus SCF complex membership, or captured in GO-CAM as the receptor arm of each ligase activity,
    rather than as bare protein binding on the invariant adaptor?
- question: Where should the boundary lie between GO:0160072 (scaffold activity, what SKP1 does) and GO:1990756 (ligase-substrate
    adaptor activity, what the F-box protein does)? Both are currently annotated to SKP1 by IDA from the same beta-TrCP1-SKP1-beta-catenin
    structure, which shows the substrate bound by the receptor.
- question: Which receptor-specific outputs (circadian period, iron sensing, TORC1 signalling, xenophagy, mitophagy, ciliogenesis,
    neuromuscular synapse assembly) should be annotated to SKP1 at all, given that a single adaptor serves ~69 receptors
    and supports opposite-sign outputs through different ones?
- question: Is the substrate-binding enhancement seen for SKP1 in the PAM/FBXO45 ligase a general property of SKP1-receptor
    pairs - so that GO:0140677 would apply across SCF - or specific to the CUL1-independent complex in which it was demonstrated?
suggested_experiments:
- hypothesis: SKP1 contributes more than passive tethering across the SCF family, measurably increasing the affinity of
    F-box receptors for their substrates as it does for FBXO45-NMNAT2.
  description: Measure substrate affinity and ubiquitination kinetics for purified receptor-substrate pairs from each F-box
    subfamily (SKP2-p27 with CKS1, BTRC-IkappaB-alpha phosphopeptide, FBXW7-cyclin E degron, FBXL3-CRY2) with and without
    SKP1, by surface plasmon resonance or ITC alongside single-turnover ubiquitin transfer, using an SCF core lacking SKP1
    as the comparator.
  experiment_type: quantitative binding and single-turnover kinetics with reconstituted ligases
- hypothesis: The mobile C-terminal loops and partly formed H7 helix of SKP1 are what allow one adaptor to accept structurally
    diverse F-box domains, so rigidifying them should restrict the receptor repertoire rather than abolish ligase activity.
  description: Introduce loop-2 and H7 substitutions and disulfide staples into SKP1, rescue SKP1-depleted cells with each
    allele, and compare the bound F-box proteome by quantitative interaction proteomics and the stability of a substrate
    panel (p27, cyclin E, IkappaB-alpha, CRY2, IRP2, CP110) by pulse-chase.
  experiment_type: structure-guided mutational rescue with interaction and degradation proteomics
- hypothesis: Nuclear retention of F-box proteins by SKP1 occupancy, not ubiquitination, accounts for part of the SKP1 loss-of-function
    phenotype.
  description: Compare SKP1 alleles that bind F-box domains but cannot bind CUL1 with wild-type SKP1 in SKP1-degron cells,
    scoring nuclear/cytoplasmic partitioning of FBXO7 and other NES-in-F-box receptors by imaging and fractionation, and
    separating that readout from substrate turnover measured in parallel.
  experiment_type: separation-of-function rescue with compartment-resolved imaging
- hypothesis: The centrosomal pool of SKP1 is recruited by specific receptors rather than by an intrinsic centrosomal determinant
    in SKP1.
  description: Quantify SKP1 at centrosomes by expansion microscopy and purified-centrosome proteomics in cells depleted
    of cyclin F, FBXW5 or FBXL13 individually and in combination, testing whether the pool collapses receptor by receptor
    or persists independently.
  experiment_type: quantitative imaging and organelle proteomics with receptor depletion
